item.title: Market Hands
item.description:
Part of an ongoing series about work done by hand. I asked first, in broken Portuguese; she said yes and went back to selling mint as if nothing had happened.

The 50mm forces you to stand at conversational distance. That’s the whole point — you can’t hide behind a long lens.

item.title: Glasshouse Geometry
item.description: A study in repetition. I walked the upper gallery three times before the geometry resolved into a frame — the trick was waiting for a cloud to soften the light so the iron stopped sparkling and started drawing lines.

item.title: Fog over Hintersee
item.description:
The alarm went off at five. By six the shore was invisible and the water had turned the colour of unbleached paper. I waited an hour for the rowboats to drift into frame, shooting maybe six frames in total.

Fog is patient. It rewards the same.

The trick with mist is to underexpose slightly — otherwise the camera tries to make everything a cheerful middle grey and the whole mood collapses.

item.title: Slow Radio
item.description: Ambient field recordings — rain, wind, looms — mixed live for production of a very calm radio station, streaming 24/7.

item.title: Concrete & Vine
item.description:
A parking structure near the harbour, photographed on an evening walk. The building’s architect reportedly hated the planting plan; the plants did not care what the architect thought.

I keep returning to places where maintenance has quietly stopped — not dereliction exactly, just the beginning of a negotiation between concrete and green.

item.title: Birch Interval
item.description:
Early spring in Finland: the light arrives at a shallow angle all morning and turns every trunk into a column of contrast.

I exposed for the bark and let the snow blow out slightly — pure white felt honest for a morning like that.

item.title: Herbarium OCR
item.description: A pipeline that digitises a local natural history society’s hand-written plant records into a searchable database.

item.title: Low Tide, Late Light
item.description:
Twenty minutes of usable light, a kilometre of exposed seabed, and no one else on the beach. These are the sessions that remind me why I carry gear up coastal paths.

Long exposure flattened the last of the waves into a single soft band — everything else is just reflection.
